commitResults.messageBody:
Renamed Duke to Jeryl to move away from the placeholder chatbot name,
per Level-0 instructions. Updated the ASCII banner and references in
README.md and docs/README.md accordingly, and filled in the student
profile placeholders in AGENTS.md, and updated the Java version setup
instructions to match this machine's actual setup (Homebrew-installed
Java 25, not sdkman).

Update main() to greet the user with the chatbot's name and purpose,
then print a farewell message before exiting, per Level-0 instructions.
No input handling yet — the chatbot still exits immediately.

Read user input in a loop and echo each line back until the user
types "bye", per Level-1 instructions. Uses a Scanner over System.in.

Store each entered line as a task in a fixed-size array (up to 100
tasks) and add a "list" command to display them with 1-based
numbering, per Level-2 instructions. No persistence to disk yet.

Track completion status for each task with a parallel boolean array
and add a "mark INDEX" command to set a task as done. "list" now
shows the [X]/[ ] status icon. No new classes introduced yet.

Add an "unmark INDEX" command that reverses a task's done status,
completing the base Level-3 requirement before introducing the
A-Classes extension.

Introduce a Task class to hold a task's description and done status,
replacing the parallel String[]/boolean[] arrays with a single
Task[] array. This is the A-Classes extension for Level-3.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for todo, deadline, and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Extend Task with a type marker and optional by/from/to fields (no
new classes yet) and parse "todo", "deadline .../by ...", and
"event .../from .../to ..." commands. Task#toString() renders the
[T]/[D]/[E] prefix and any date/time info. Dates/times are kept as
plain strings for now.

Introduce Todo, Deadline, and Event as subclasses of Task, replacing
the type-flag field and by/from/to fields on Task itself. Each
subclass overrides toString() to render its own type prefix and
detail suffix. This is the A-Inheritance extension for Level-4.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle minimal errors: empty todo, unknown command
commitResults.messageBody:
Print an OOPS!!! message instead of crashing when a "todo" command
has no description, or when the input doesn't match any known
command, per the minimal Level-5 requirement.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JerylException and comprehensive error handling
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a custom JerylException and use try/catch around command
processing so no input can crash the program. Covers: empty todo/
deadline/event descriptions, missing /by or /from+/to, missing or
non-numeric or out-of-range task numbers for mark/unmark, and unknown
commands. This is the A-Exceptions extension for Level-5 (typical
level: all current commands covered).

Add a "delete INDEX" command that removes a task from the array,
shifting later entries down. Reuses the existing parseTaskIndex
validation, so an invalid or missing index is reported gracefully.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use ArrayList instead of a fixed-size array
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace Task[100] + manual taskCount bookkeeping with ArrayList<Task>,
removing the artificial 100-task cap and the manual shift-down loop
in delete. This is the A-Collections extension for Level-6.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use an enum for command dispatch
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a Command enum (LIST, MARK, UNMARK, DELETE, TODO, DEADLINE,
EVENT, BYE, UNKNOWN) and switch on it instead of a long chain of
String startsWith/equals checks. Each command's logic is extracted
into its own private method for readability. This is the A-Enums
extension.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Storage for saving/loading tasks to disk
commitResults.messageBody:
Each Task subclass now knows how to encode itself as a single
pipe-delimited line (e.g. "T | 1 | read book"), and Storage can
write a task list to ./data/jeryl.txt and parse it back. Storage
creates the data folder if missing, treats a missing file as an
empty task list, and skips corrupted lines with a warning instead
of crashing on startup.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wire Storage into Jeryl: load on startup, save on every change
commitResults.messageBody:
Jeryl now loads tasks from ./data/jeryl.txt at startup and saves
the full task list after every command that mutates it (mark,
unmark, delete, todo, deadline, event), so the list survives a
restart. Ignore the generated ./data/ folder in git since it's
runtime state, not source.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parse deadline/event dates as LocalDate instead of plain strings
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline.by and Event.from/to are now java.time.LocalDate rather
than String. User input must be yyyy-mm-dd (e.g. 2019-10-15), and
is echoed back in a friendlier "MMM dd yyyy" format (e.g. Oct 15
2019). Bad date input now produces a clear JerylException instead
of being stored as an opaque string.

Storage.parseLine and the file format are updated to match: dates
round-trip through the save file using LocalDate's ISO string form
(yyyy-MM-dd), and a corrupted date on disk is reported and skipped
like any other malformed line, rather than crashing on load.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui class for all user-facing console interaction
commitResults.messageBody:
Jeryl previously mixed input reading and every printed message
directly into its command-handling logic. Move all of that into a
new Ui class (banner/welcome, goodbye, error, and the per-command
result messages, plus reading command lines from stdin), so Jeryl
now delegates to ui.showXyz(...) rather than calling
System.out.println directly. This is the first step of extracting
Duke's classic Ui/Storage/Parser/TaskList structure out of the one
big class; Storage already existed, Parser and TaskList are next.

TaskList wraps the ArrayList<Task> that used to be passed around
directly, exposing add/delete/get/size, so command handlers work
with a task list abstraction rather than a raw collection.

Parser.parse(String) takes over splitting a raw input line into a
Command and its argument string (previously done inline in
Jeryl's main loop), returning a small ParsedInput record.

Jeryl's main method is now much closer to the target Duke-style
skeleton: read a line, parse it, dispatch to a handler that
operates on the TaskList via Ui for output and Storage for
persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: Organize classes into packages under jeryl
commitResults.messageBody:
Splits the previously flat src/main/java into sub-packages by
responsibility, going straight for the stretch goal since the
class count already warrants it:

- jeryl: Jeryl (entry point), TaskList
- jeryl.task: Task, Todo, Deadline, Event
- jeryl.ui: Ui
- jeryl.storage: Storage
- jeryl.parser: Parser, Command
- jeryl.exception: JerylException

src/main/java remains the source root (unchanged), as required.
The app's main class is now jeryl.Jeryl; run/compile commands and
any IDE run configuration need to reference that instead of the
old top-level Jeryl.

commitResults.messageTitle: build.gradle: Point application/shadowJar at jeryl.Jeryl, not seedu.duke.Duke
commitResults.messageBody:
The add-gradle-support branch's build.gradle was written for the
unmodified Duke template (class Duke in package seedu.duke). This
project's entry point is jeryl.Jeryl (see A-Packages), so update
mainClass accordingly and rename the shadow JAR output to
jeryl.jar to match. Verified with `./gradlew build` and
`./gradlew run` (piping sample commands through stdin) that the
app builds and runs correctly under Gradle with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for the core logic classes
commitResults.messageBody:
Covers the non-trivial public methods across the classes with the
most business logic, going beyond the two-method minimum:

- Command.fromKeyword: known/unknown/case-insensitive/empty input
- Parser.parse: command/argument splitting, no-args, unknown
  command, multiple spaces
- TaskList: add, delete (incl. out-of-bounds), size
- Todo/Deadline/Event: toString and toFileString formatting,
  including date parsing/printing edge cases (single-digit day)
- Storage: save/load round trip, missing file, missing parent
  folder auto-creation, and skipping a corrupted line while still
  loading the valid ones around it

Storage tests use JUnit's @TempDir so they exercise real file I/O
without touching the project's own ./data folder or leaving files
behind. Run with `./gradlew test`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
"find <keyword>" lists all tasks whose description contains the
keyword (case-insensitive substring match), preserving their
original list order/numbering isn't reused -- matches are
renumbered from 1, matching the sample output in the spec.

TaskList.find(keyword) returns a new TaskList of the matches;
Ui.showMatchingTasks prints them under the required header. Task
gained a getDescription() getter so the search doesn't need to
parse it back out of toString().

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc comments to public classes/constructors/methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Covers every previously-undocumented public class, constructor,
and method across the codebase: Jeryl (class + main), TaskList's
constructors/add/delete/get/size, Ui's constructor and every
showXyz message method, Parser.parse, Task/Todo/Deadline/Event
constructors, and JerylException's constructor. Storage's private
parseDate also got a comment since its behavior (wrapping a parse
failure as a JerylException) isn't obvious from its signature.

No behavior changed; verified with `./gradlew test`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Wrap a line exceeding the 120-char hard limit
commitResults.messageBody:
Reviewed the codebase against the SE-EDU Java coding standard
(se-education.org/guides/conventions/java/intermediate.html):
naming, indentation, brace style, operator/comma whitespace,
import ordering (no wildcards, static/java.*/jeryl.* groups with
blank lines between), and Javadoc phrasing already comply. The
only violation found was one line over the 120-character hard
limit in addEvent's error message, which this wraps using the
standard's 8-space continuation indent.

Going forward, new code in this project should follow this
standard too.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/jeryl/task/Task.java
#	src/main/java/jeryl/ui/Ui.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JavaFX GUI entry point (Level-10 part 1: getting started)
commitResults.messageBody:
Follows the SE-EDU JavaFX tutorial's first step: Main extends
Application and shows a "Hello World" Scene/Stage; Launcher is a
plain main() that calls Application.launch(Main.class, args), used
as the actual entry point to work around a JavaFX/fat-jar
classpath issue. mainClass in build.gradle now points at
jeryl.Launcher instead of jeryl.Jeryl.

Deviated from the tutorial's build.gradle snippet in one way: it
depends on every OS/arch classifier (win/mac/mac-aarch64/linux) of
each javafx-* artifact at once, which sounds necessary for a
cross-platform JAR but actually breaks at runtime -- the per-OS
JARs share native-library resource paths, so JavaFX's extractor
can unpack the wrong OS/arch's binary (reproduced here: it tried
loading an x86_64 mac .dylib built for the win classifier on this
Apple Silicon machine, since all four JARs were on the classpath
simultaneously). Instead, build.gradle now detects the running
machine's OS/arch and depends on only the matching classifier.
Trade-off: `./gradlew shadowJar` now produces a JAR that only runs
on the OS/arch it was built on, not a true cross-platform JAR;
revisit if cross-platform distribution is needed later.

Verified: `./gradlew run` opens the Hello World window without
error (native libs load correctly for mac-aarch64), and
`./gradlew test` / `./gradlew shadowJar` still succeed -- the
existing CLI code (jeryl.Jeryl) and its tests are untouched.

commitResults.messageTitle: Build the JavaFX chat GUI (tutorial parts 2-5), wired to real Jeryl logic
commitResults.messageBody:
Implements the SE-EDU JavaFX tutorial's full chat window directly
in its final FXML-based form, rather than keeping the intermediate
non-FXML versions from parts 2-3 around:

- MainWindow.java / MainWindow.fxml: the main window (ScrollPane +
  VBox of dialog bubbles, TextField, Send button), auto-scrolling
  via a binding on the dialog container's height.
- DialogBox.java / DialogBox.fxml: a reusable chat bubble
  (Label + ImageView), loaded via fx:root so it can be built
  programmatically; getJerylDialog() flips it to the left so
  Jeryl's replies are visually distinct from the user's.
- Main.java: JavaFX entry point, loads MainWindow.fxml, links
  main.css, and injects a Jeryl instance into the controller.
- src/main/resources/css/main.css: chat-bubble/input/button
  styling with hover/focus states (tutorial part 5).

Rather than bundling real image assets for the avatars, they are
generated at runtime as plain colored circles (MainWindow's
createAvatar) -- keeps the repo free of binary files for what's
just a placeholder, and is trivial to swap for real artwork later.

To let the GUI reuse the exact same command-handling logic as the
CLI (instead of a toy "echo" stub like the tutorial's throwaway
Duke class), Jeryl and Ui were refactored:

- Jeryl is now instance-based, with public getResponse(String) and
  isExit(String) methods. main()'s CLI loop is now a thin wrapper
  (runCli()) that calls getResponse() and prints the result -- the
  command dispatch/validation logic itself is unchanged.
- Ui's showXyz(...) methods (which printed directly) became
  xyzMessage(...) methods that return the formatted String instead.
  This lets both the CLI (which prints the string) and the GUI
  (which puts it in a DialogBox) use identical message text without
  duplicating any formatting logic.

Verified: `./gradlew test` (all existing tests pass unchanged --
none of them touched Ui's printing, so the refactor was invisible
to them), a manual CLI run producing byte-identical output to
before the refactor, and `./gradlew run` launching without any
FXML-loading or native-library errors (confirmed via logs; a
screenshot of the live window could not be captured in this
session's environment, so the visual layout is unverified pending
a manual check).
